page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor platform. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of RAM. This provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio (2.0 GB per vCPU). Hardware capabilities include 32 MB of L3 cache alongside advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512 (f, vnni, bf16) and cryptographic hardware acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, lacks local ephemeral storage, and contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Performance data highlights strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core benchmarks and Geekbench single-core scores (1973.0) placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Text processing performance is similarly strong. Multi-core CPU metrics fall into the middle 50% category, indicated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4481.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 7535.23. Read-heavy memory bandwidth tests, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rank in the lower 25% of benchmarks.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio establishes qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require strong per-core computational speed without requiring large memory footprints or high IOPS local storage. Relying on network storage and 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, the ecs.c8a.xlarge presents tradeoffs in memory throughput and multi-threaded scaling. Recommended application fits include light web serving, single-threaded batch execution tasks, text processing, and low-concurrency compute jobs.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor operating at 2.7 GHz. Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of RAM, and 32 MB of L3 cache, it delivers strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25% for single-thread benchmark suites and text processing tasks. The instance includes AVX-512 extensions and cryptographic instruction sets, supported by a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no local storage or hardware GPU acceleration. While multi-core CPU results and memory write bandwidth are average, memory read bandwidth and multi-threaded software compilation exhibit lower relative metrics. Featuring a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.c8a.xlarge provides cost-effective resource utilization for single-threaded processing, light text analysis, and modest compute tasks, though high-concurrency database operations and memory-bound workloads are limited by its memory profile.
